title: Vegas Golden Knights: What to Expect from the 2026-27 Season
subtitle: New pieces and a different head coach promise to transform the team in pursuit of the Stanley Cup Finals.
excerpt: With a new coach, key trades, and veteran additions, the Vegas Golden Knights enter the 2026-27 season looking to return to Stanley Cup contention after the.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The Vegas Golden Knights enter the 2026-27 season after losing the Stanley Cup Final in six games to the Hurricanes. The franchise seeks to return to its championship path with changes to the roster and coaching staff.

New coaching direction

Ryan Craig takes over as head coach, replacing the previous coach. The change aims to bring more consistency to the style of play and improve the defensive transition, areas identified as vulnerable during the last campaign.

Reconfiguring the offense

The team traded Pavel Dorofeyev to the New York Rangers, in addition to losing Keegan Kolesar and Colton Sissons, who made up the depth line. On the other hand, the club re-signed Victor Olofsson, added Marc Gatcomb as a free agent, and expects Braeden Bowman to play the full season after splitting time between the AHL and Vegas.

Focus on defense and goaltending

To strengthen the defensive line, Vegas traded Kaeden Korczak for Parker Wotherspoon and maintained an experienced core. The club also added veteran William Karlsson, who returns from injury after missing 68 games, to bring leadership and two-way play. Goaltending is still seen as a weak point, and the team may need changes before the trade deadline.

Key players

William Karlsson is highlighted as a key player, offering consistent production and physical presence. The expectation is that he will return to the 50-point level he maintained throughout his career. In addition to him, trust is placed in Trevor Connelly, who could get minutes in case of injuries, and in youngsters like Braeden Bowman, who are looking to establish themselves in the league.

Predictions and goals

Analysts suggest that the defense will be the most vulnerable area, potentially leading to moves in the market before the trade deadline. Even so, the prediction is for the team to reach the playoffs as a Wild Card, maintaining the ambition to reach the Stanley Cup Finals once again.
